sections.html:
Payments are taken at 200 E 4th Street in Woodbine, and mail goes to PO Box 698. The phone is 912-576-3248, and the counter is open 9 to 5 on weekdays. Valuation is a separate department. The assessors, who are appointed by the county commissioners, take valuation questions at 912-576-3241.

If you are selling, one statement from the tax commissioner's page is worth remembering: the office plays no part in dividing the year's tax between buyer and seller, and liability stays with the owner. Your closing attorney or title company works out the split and asks the office for the amount owed on the parcel.

sections.h2: When the bill arrives and when it is due
sections.html:
Bills leave the county in mid-September, and payment is due 60 days after the mail-out. The bill goes to whoever held title on January 1 of that tax year, so if you sold afterward, pass the notice along to the new owner. If nothing has reached your mailbox by October 15, call 912-576-3248.

The state Department of Revenue's Camden fact sheet gives December 20 as the standard statewide due date and says a county may move it or bill in installments. It also allows every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark before interest begins. Camden's own schedule controls, so go by the date printed on your statement.

sections.h2: Late charges and how a lien builds
sections.html:
Delinquency starts the day after the due date. Interest runs at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent a year, any part of a month counts as a whole month, and at least $1 is owed (O.C.G.A. 48-5-148). A flat 5% penalty applies at 120 days overdue, and again at 240, 360 and 480 (O.C.G.A. 48-2-44). Homestead bills of $500 or less escape the penalty, and so do new owners who lived outside Georgia, never received a bill and pay within a year.

What follows a missed Camden County due date
WhenWhat happens
Day after the due dateInterest begins
Week after the due date30-day lien warning is mailed
About a week after the warning period endsLien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, adding a filing cost of $28.50 to $33.50
120, 240, 360 and 480 days overdue5% penalty each time
After filingA tax sale can be scheduled

sections.h2: Can I get my house back after a tax sale?
sections.html:
Yes, for a limited time. The lien reaches back to the January 1 valuation (O.C.G.A. 48-2-56) and outranks every other lien. Each December 31 the tax commissioner must issue an execution against delinquent accounts (O.C.G.A. 48-3-3), which directs the levying officer to collect or to levy and sell.

Redeeming costs the winning bid, plus any later taxes the buyer covered, plus 20% of that sum for the first year or fraction of a year. Each added year or fraction adds another 10%. After twelve months the buyer may serve notice to cut off redemption for good (O.C.G.A. 48-4-45 through 48-4-48), and the earliest a buyer can take physical control is one year and forty-five days after the deed.

Given that timeline, selling before the sale date usually keeps more equity in your pocket than waiting does.

A Notice of Reassessment starts a 45-day clock. Send your appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, and make sure it is postmarked inside that window. Assessed value is 40% of the January 1 market value, so when market value climbs, assessed value follows.

Overpayment has its own route. A written refund request for tax assessed or collected in error can be made within three years of payment.

  • Returns go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • Homestead applications are taken year-round, but April 1 is the cutoff for that year.
  • Skipping the application is treated as waiving the exemption.

Pull together deeds, survey papers and any receipts for improvements before you apply or appeal, so the office can match its records to your file in one visit.

sections.h2: Do Kingsland, St. Marys and Woodbine send their own tax bills?
sections.html:
Possibly, and it depends on where the house sits. Cities levy their own ad valorem tax and the city clerk bills and collects it, unless the city and county have agreed to put everything on one county statement. Only the county tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax in any Georgia county.

Ask the Woodbine tax office whether your address carries a separate city bill, and ask the city clerk for any city balance, since an unpaid city tax can hold up a closing just as a county one does.

The state fact sheet adds two rules that matter around a purchase. A mobile home needs a county location permit within 30 days of placement and again each January 1 to April 1. A long-term note secured by real estate must be recorded in the county within 90 days, with intangible recording tax of $1.50 for each $500 of the note.

sections.h2: What Camden's housing market looks like
sections.html:
Camden fills Georgia's southeastern corner, with Glynn County to the north and Nassau County in Florida to the south. Kingsland is the biggest city, St. Marys and Woodbine are the others, and Interstate 95 and U.S. 17 run through the county. The Navy's submarine base at Kings Bay anchors much of the local housing demand, and Cumberland Island National Seashore is part of the county.

The July 2025 estimate is 60,143 residents. Owners live in 67.8% of homes, the median owned home is worth $261,400, median monthly rent is $1,235, and 446 permits for new housing were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: Steps to settle taxes when you sell
sections.html:
Call the Woodbine tax office at 912-576-3248 for the balance on your parcel and ask whether any earlier year is open. If the house is inside a city, ask the city clerk for that bill as well. Give both figures to your closing attorney or title company, who will pay them from your proceeds and divide the current year between you and the buyer.

Do not wait for the bill if it has not come. Interest builds even when a statement never arrives, so call early. A cash sale moves faster than a financed one, and the tax figures are needed just the same.

faqs.q: Does the Woodbine tax office divide the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: No. The office takes no part in prorating, and liability attaches to the owner. Your closing attorney or title company handles the split using the balance the office confirms.

faqs.q: I never received a Camden County statement. What now?
faqs.a: Call 912-576-3248. The county asks owners who have nothing by October 15 to get in touch. Interest still builds on a late balance even if the bill never reached you.

faqs.q: How fast does a Camden County lien follow a missed due date?
faqs.a: A 30-day notice is mailed the week after the due date, and the lien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court about a week after that. The $28.50 to $33.50 filing cost is added to your bill.

faqs.q: After a Camden County tax sale, can the owner redeem?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the buyer's price plus 20% for the first year and 10% for each later year. The right ends only after the buyer completes the notice steps that bar redemption, which can begin twelve months after the sale.

faqs.q: Is there a late penalty on a small Camden County homestead bill?
faqs.a: The 5% penalty is waived when the homestead tax is $500 or less. Interest still applies at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, with a $1 minimum.
